samples.summary: Peer-supplied `lineAffinity` from Yorkie presence is consumed unvalidated in the local render path
samples.evidence: `peer.position.lineAffinity` (editor.ts, peer caret loop) and `pos.lineAffinity` in `scrollToPosition` now flow straight into `resolvePositionPixel`, whose value originates in `p.presence.activeCursorPos` built with a non-null assertion and no shape check in packages/frontend/src/app/docs/docs-view.tsx:226 (and :243 for jumpToPeer). A hostile collaborator on the same Yorkie document fully controls that object, so `lineAffinity` can be any JSON value, not just 'forward' | 'backward'. Traced the vector to its end: the value is only used in strict equality tests (`affinity === 'forward'` in peer-cursor.ts:206 and pagination.ts:401), so a bogus value degrades to backward rendering — no injection, no memory/loop hazard, no secret exposure. Reported as defence-in-depth only: the untrusted presence payload (blockId/offset/lineAffinity) crosses the trust boundary into the layout engine with no validation at the boundary, and this change widens the set of presence fields the renderer trusts.

samples.summary: `recordHistoryPresence` publishes the caret to presence without the `clampPosToModel` guard `updateCursorPos` applies
samples.evidence: `updateCursorPos` (yorkie-doc-store.ts:2995) deliberately clamps before publishing so 'an out-of-model offset ... never leaks into peer presence', but `recordHistoryPresence` writes `activeCursorPos: cursor` (line 2906) unclamped, where `cursor` is the raw `pendingCursorPos` staged by `setCursorForHistory` (line 2882, unclamped) or a hand-built post-edit position. This change re-types that parameter to a full `DocPosition`, so the field now carries the caret's affinity through this unguarded path too. Impact is limited to a peer receiving an offset past block length (rendering falls back / returns undefined) — no sensitive content is in a DocPosition — so this is hardening, not a leak of secret data. Pre-existing path; not introduced by this diff.
